campaign: Brand and performance marketing mix shift
objective: Reduce dependence on paid performance acquisition by strengthening brand, communications and direct or unpaid traffic.
businessContext: COVID-19 disrupted travel demand while paid search competition and brand-keyword costs created pressure on acquisition economics.
strategy: Shift the mix toward brand and communications, reduce performance marketing relative to 2019 and coordinate product launches with integrated marketing.
execution: Paused portions of performance spend during the pandemic
outcomes: Airbnb disclosed a $661.8 million decline in combined brand and performance marketing in 2020, including a $540.5 million decline in performance marketing.
The filing states the strategy and risks but does not establish a causal lift from the mix shift.
whatWorked: The allocation thesis considered direct demand and brand strength rather than treating every booking as a paid-media outcome.
whatFailed: Pandemic demand shocks make simple before-and-after efficiency claims unreliable.
transferConditions: The brand already has meaningful direct demand and can measure incrementality, repeat rate and channel overlap.
nonTransferConditions: Do not cut performance spend merely because a famous brand did; test marginal return and demand capture first.

sources.title: Airbnb 2020 Form 10-K
sources.methodology: Company filing states the media-mix change, spend movements and risks; COVID-19 is a major confounder.
